candidate.title: CapSeq
candidate.scope: Assigned middle poster row: CapSeq, captioned 5′ anchored profiling of Pol II transcripts (CapSeq), interpreted as the longer-capped-RNA implementation described by Gu et al. (2012). Visible inventory: mixed Total RNA end classes P/OH/PPP/GPPP → Terminator → CIP → TAP → Primer Ligation → Random Primer → Reverse transcription → Purification → cDNA. The upper surviving 5′ OH class and lower cap-derived class are retained through the depicted chemistry and priming. Frag-seq above and CIP-TAP below are neighboring independently labeled workflows, not connected alternatives or targets of this CapSeq card. The left highlighted capped-RNA glyph is a target illustration; it is not a cap-binding isolation step. This extraction ends at the depicted purified cDNA and uses primary-paper information to explain the downstream library/readout interface, without reconstructing unshown execution.

states.label: Purified cDNA
features: Single blue cDNA line is the depicted endpoint; no sequencing instrument or data-analysis branch is drawn.
DNA is the readout carrier for RNA-derived sequence; the original cap is not sequenced as a chemical modification.
The primary implementation subsequently yields an Illumina-adapter-amplified library of 5′ anchored tags from longer capped RNAs, including RNAs with or without poly(A) tails.
Capped transcript ends can nominate transcription start sites, but capped processed/trans-spliced RNA ends are also captured; the endpoint is not proof that every tag is a primary initiation site.
Biochemical enrichment reduces structural/uncapped RNA background; the schematic does not establish perfect specificity.

operations.label: Terminator
operations.description: Treat total RNA with Terminator exonuclease. The depicted 5′ P class is depleted, leaving 5′ OH, 5′ PPP and capped RNA in the surviving preparation.
operations.mechanism: End-dependent exonucleolytic selection; the primary paper identifies rRNA depletion as its purpose.
operations.information_effect: Reduces abundant uncapped structural RNA background before cap-derived termini are made ligatable.

operations.label: CIP
operations.description: Dephosphorylate uncapped phosphorylated surviving RNA. The 5′ PPP class becomes part of the 5′ OH background, while capped RNA retains GPPP.
operations.mechanism: Calf intestine phosphatase removes exposed 5′ phosphates; the diagram preserves the capped class.
operations.information_effect: Suppresses later 5′ adapter ligation to initially uncapped RNA without removing the capped-end target.

operations.label: TAP
operations.description: Remove the cap from the remaining capped RNA, exposing 5′ monophosphate at its original capped terminus. The background 5′ OH class persists.
operations.mechanism: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase decapping, interpreted with the depicted GPPP → P end-group change.
operations.information_effect: Converts prior cap status into a ligatable RNA terminus; the order after CIP distinguishes the target from dephosphorylated uncapped RNA.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven operations are local instances along the middle CapSeq row, with its stated Terminator→CIP→TAP preparation history. Parallel chemical glyphs are constituents/fates within a common total-RNA preparation, not evidence of separate tubes, a split, or pooling; each mixed state explicitly preserves both capped-derived and uncapped survivors. Enzymes are catalysts described in operations, while incorporated adapter and primer are material inputs. Gu full text resolves the random-primer adapter interface and longer capped-RNA readout. The broad Purification caption remains broad; the paper-reported size selection/amplification is downstream interpretive context. Page 86 is a conflicting secondary catalogue lead headed for CXXC affinity CAP-seq; page 87 targets CIP-TAP. Neither adds a target, a physical RNAPII attachment, or a CapSeq affinity-purification step. No equivalence or development relationship to the neighboring assays is asserted.
